Privacy-first on-device OCR for the Mon language (mnw), spoken by ~1 million people across Myanmar and Thailand.\n\nRecognition runs locally. A scan leaves your device only if you send it yourself through Feedback or Contribute.

Primary: Mon script (Myanmar Extended + Mon codepoints)
Secondary: Burmese, English, digits, punctuation

Charset: 315 characters (NFC-normalised)
Mon (mnw) is a vulnerable language. MonOCR aims to bridge the gap between physical texts and digital data.

Text recognition (OCR) runs entirely on your device. The images and PDFs you scan, and the text read from them, are not sent anywhere.\n\nMonOCR has no account, no analytics and no advertising. The only data it sends is what you submit through Feedback or Contribute, described in section 3.

Images you pick or capture are read on your device by the bundled model, using the device\'s neural network API (NNAPI) where it is available and the CPU otherwise. The original image and the extracted text stay on your device, in the app\'s scan history.

Feedback and Contribute are the only features that send data. When you submit one, after ticking its consent box, MonOCR uploads the file you attached, its file name and the text you entered to the MonOCR feedback service, which keeps them to check and improve the model. The upload starts right after you submit, and is retried in the background when you are online.\n\nNothing is sent before you submit. Deleting an entry from the in-app history does not remove a copy that was already uploaded. A copy of the app built without a feedback-service key keeps submissions on the device.

To maintain our strict privacy compliance, we do not use third-party cloud crash reporters. Diagnostic logs are written to your local file system on a rolling basis. You are in full control of these logs and can export them voluntarily if you encounter bugs.
If what the app sends changes, this policy will be updated in the app and in our open source repositories.
If you have any questions about this privacy statement, please contact the MonDevHub engineering team via our public open source repositories on GitHub.
